rv.q: La Barrie's excellent production proves it has never lost its relevance.
This production is a flamboyant celebration of queerness.
The production — pleasingly elevated by Rajha Shakiry’s elegant, wooden-panelled design — starts to gain pace as the central plot surrounding the blackmail of Chiké Okonkwo’s Sir Robert unfolds.
La Barrie nails the heady rush of wealthy excess.
I found the pacing quite perfect in this dynamic and pinpointedly sharp production.
You cannot help feeling Wilde would be delighted with this very modern puncturing of the balloon of political pomposity.
Wilde’s pertinent dissection of truth and hypocrisy is heightened by a fusion of Edwardian style and contemporary glamour.
La Barrie’s production is simultaneously reverential and daring, elegant and gutsy, demonstrating just how easily Wilde’s themes continue to flourish in such a fresh context.
Overall, An Ideal Husband was funny and witty, but it still needs a little more polishing.

cn.t: Critics praise this fresh, vibrant revival of Wilde's comedy, celebrating its compelling contemporary staging, flamboyant performances, and all-Black cast that brings the satire thrillingly to life with lavish costumes and energetic style.
